findings.claim: The course intake's Concept-day allocation for S20 (authoring/evidence/html-css-js/intake.md, section Block allocation per day) schedules topic videos only in the 8-minute Short video block, 'topic videos whose runtimes sum to 8 minutes or less across the day (a video that does not fit is recorded absent with the reason)'. The four S20 companions assign 7.30 (semantic), 2.22 (forms), 7.57 (accessibility) and 8.37 (box model) optional watch minutes, 25.46 minutes in all, so at most one or two of them fit the block. This 7.30-minute whole-video assignment alone nearly fills the block, so the S20 set as a whole cannot be scheduled as the intake describes.
findings.recommendation: Make the S20 day-level choice explicit: either keep only the video(s) that fit 8 minutes (the 2.22-minute forms video plus at most one short segment) and record the others absent with the reason the intake prescribes, or trim this assignment to a sub-segment (for example the heading-outline part, 0:00 to 4:45, which serves o2 best) and get the intake amended to treat companions as unscheduled extra time.

findings.claim: The creator description carries no timestamp chapters and the player metadata exposes none, yet the companion says the coverage and its minute ranges come 'Per its chapters, description and captions' and the cautions say fit was judged from 'the chapters'. A learner or reviewer cannot tell where the segment boundaries come from.
findings.recommendation: Say where the time ranges come from (YouTube auto-generated key moments, or caption timestamps) and drop 'chapters' wherever the creator published none, in both the body line and the cautions.
